requirement.target: 0 damaged files in 10,000 randomized kill-during-save trials, including power-loss emulation; previous file intact on every failure.
requirement.review_state: Partial for the concrete returned-error gap: when directory fsync fails after replacement rename, the writer returns Err after replacing the previous destination; that prior version is neither restored nor retained durably. The 20,000 randomized SIGKILL trials and five fixed QEMU power-loss controls validate only the frozen current Linux writer and do not cover this injected directory-sync error path. The controls are one Linux/ext4/virtio-blk setup; current Windows directory sync is a no-op and no Windows namespace-durability or power-loss guarantee has been established.

production_writer.description: Same-directory temporary write, file fsync, atomic rename, directory fsync on Unix. Both SIGKILL campaigns and the QEMU guest writer used this source revision.

randomized_sigkill_campaigns.filesystem: Local ext4 under runs/continuation; the two writer campaigns ran sequentially.

execution_limits.verification_note: The recorded runner script passes the listed limits to systemd-run --user; the two services completed successfully. Their transient unit files were collected after exit, and no independent active-time ceiling snapshot was retained, so the post-run show defaults are not used as evidence of the live limits.

power_loss_emulation.platform_scope: One QEMU TCG Linux guest on ext4 over virtio-blk with dm-log-writes; one fixed cut at each named production-writer boundary; log prefixes replayed on a pristine baseline and mounted for recovery.
power_loss_emulation.scope_note: These five fixed-cut power-loss controls are separate from, and not counted among, the two 10,000-trial randomized SIGKILL campaigns. Rename permits either complete old or new content; OLD was observed.

interpretation.data_integrity: Both current-writer randomized campaigns completed 10,000 trials with 0 damaged files and 0 not-run trials. All five fixed QEMU power-loss controls recovered a fully checksummed OLD or NEW payload.
interpretation.temporary_cleanup: SIGKILL campaigns reported leftover temporary files (1,643 shared writer; 5,345 study writer). This is a cleanup concern, separate from whether the destination file was damaged; the campaigns classified 0 damaged destination files.
interpretation.other_write_paths: Evidence-store blobs and interface-check/extraction streaming writes remain separate non-atomic scratch or materialization paths and are not covered by these save-destination campaigns.
interpretation.criterion_scope: The written target does not require 10,000 separate VM cuts or repetitions on every OS. Evidence consists of two current-writer 10,000-trial randomized SIGKILL campaigns on local ext4 and five fixed QEMU power-loss cuts across the writer boundaries in one guest/filesystem/device setup. The concrete remaining gap is the destination state after a post-rename directory-sync error: the call returns an error after replacing the old name, but the writer keeps no durable previous version and does not attempt rollback. This violates the explicit previous-file-intact-on-every-failure clause; REL-010 remains Partial for that reason. Current Windows directory sync is a no-op; no Windows namespace-durability or power-loss guarantee has been established, and the Unix/QEMU results do not apply to Windows.
interpretation.post_rename_failure: On Existing::Replace, a failure from sync_directory after rename returns Err while the new complete file may occupy the destination and old bytes are unavailable. The protocol has no durable backup or rollback. This is not a damaged/partial destination in the campaign tally, but it does fail the requirement that the previous file remain intact on every failure.
interpretation.next_protocol: Make a same-directory previous-version copy durable before replacement; on the post-rename sync error, attempt a durable rollback while keeping the backup name. If rollback fails, return an error that names the retained recovery copy. Preserve no-clobber for Existing::Refuse and stream the copy with bounded memory.
interpretation.platform_limit: The frozen production writer uses a no-op directory sync on Windows. No Windows durability control was run; REL-010 is not established for Windows.
